summary: ```# Marvelous Designer 2024: Feature Overview ## Introduction In Marvelous Designer 2024, several new features enhance the user experience for creating stunning virtual garments. From wind simulation to LiveSync capabilities, this overview will detail the significant updates and functionalities available in this version. ## Wind Controller In Marvelous Designer 2024, you can now set up multiple wind sources to create a more natural and richer wind environment. To access this feature, go to the environment icon in the 3D window and click on **Wind Controller**. ### Duplicating Wind Controllers To duplicate a wind controller, right-click on the controller's shape and select **Duplicate**. Record the simulation cache to see the results. ### Unlimited Bound Unlimited Bound is activated by default and creates a global wind. If Unlimited Bound is turned off, the wind force will be limited to the Bound area, functioning as a local wind with restricted effect. ## Video Capture Feature With the **Video Capture** feature, you can capture a quick preview of the animation shown in the 3D window. Play in real-time and save the output as a video file. This tool is located under the **Main Menu > Animation > Video Capture** and the **Animation Editor** toolbar. ### Capturing Video Click the **Capture** button to start. When executing Capture, the button will change into a **Stop** button, allowing you to terminate the capture process. Once the capture ends, the video will automatically launch in your default media player. ## Soft Body Simulation The **Soft Body Simulation** feature applies deformable body simulations to express self-reflection. This option is available only for Marvelous Designer's default avatar types. ### Setting Up Soft Body Simulation To use Soft Body Simulation for custom avatars, you must use the **Auto-Convert to Avatar** function, which will be demonstrated later in this video. Select the avatar in the 3D window and go to the **Property Editor** to turn on Soft Body Simulation. Set the **Soft Body Stiffness** value; the smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. ### Recording Soft Body Animation When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right-hand corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. Record the animation while Soft Body Simulation is active. A new layer is created and recorded separately, and this animation cache can be exported in **Alembic** format. ## Auto-Convert Avatar Feature With the **Auto-Convert Avatar** feature, you can automatically convert avatars created in other software to the default avatar in Marvelous Designer. ### Converting Avatars Click **Main Menu > Avatar > Auto-Convert to Avatar**. In the pop-up window, load a character in **AVT**, **OBJ**, or **FBX** file format. Select the desired gender of the avatar. ### Conversion Options - **Automatic or Custom**: Maintains the current rig. - **MD Skin Style**: Maintains the body shape of the original file while converting the appearance to a CLO avatar and adding joints. - **Rigging**: Only adds joints while maintaining both the body shape and appearance of the original file. - **Size Editable**: Changes the avatar's body shape and adds joints in Marvelous Designer to allow for size editing while keeping the original avatar intact. The converted avatar will appear in the 3D window, granting access to features like Motion and Soft Body Simulation. ## Everywhere Feature The **Everywhere** feature connects creators' digital outfits to all avatars and digital spaces. It allows for easy optimization of outfits to suit digital environments such as games and the metaverse. ### Optimization Features Features include: - **Mesh Optimization** - **Rigging** - **UV Packing** - **Texture Baking** ### Polygon Count Optimization To optimize the polygon count of the garment, enter the target polygon count and click on the **Polygon Count icon**. After that, click **Optimize** to adjust the outfit's polygons. ### Individual Trim Optimization For individual trim optimization, select the button or trim from the Object Browser. Input your target polygon count in the **Face Count** under the **LOD** menu in the Property Editor. ### Trim Billboarding You can minimize the trim mesh count using trim billboarding by checking the **Plane** option, which converts the trim into an image. For quad mesh preferences, select the mesh option and click the mesh button. Then, choose the **Optimize Quad** option under the Mesh menu in the Property Editor. ## Rigging with Everywhere Tool For rigging outfits, click the **Rigging Apply** option in the garment tab. This automatically rigs the outfit, revealing update and brush tools. ### Weight Painting Hold **Control** and click on a joint to inspect the weights associated with it in the 3D window. Weight painting can be done in both the 3D and 2D windows using brushes to add, subtract, or smooth weight values. ### Sculpting If you notice your outfit has holes or overlaps, use the **Sculpt Brush** to adjust its shape. The Sculpt Brush offers two blend modes: **grab** and **smooth**, toggled by pressing **Control + Tab**. ## UV Packing Switching to the material tab, **UV Packing** automatically lays out UVs without overlapping, allowing for the organization of many UVs at once. In the UV packing window, input the desired configuration and click **Apply** to pack the UVs into the selected tile. ## Texture Baking The **Texture Baking** feature generates maps that represent the details of a high poly model onto an optimized model. In the Everywhere texture baking window, check the detail normal map and ambient occlusion maps. ### Adjusting Ray Sample Count The ray sample count for the ambient occlusion map is the number of rays sampled per pixel. You can adjust the intensity of the normal map using the slider. ## Uploading to Kinect When ready to upload your file to Kinect, click the upload button at the bottom of the Everywhere window and adjust the options, then click **OK**. You'll be directed to the Kinect upload webpage, and the file will be uploaded to CloseSight Kinect. ### Downloading FBX Files Click the **FBX download button** to download the garment's FBX file. ## LiveSync **LiveSync** is a bridge that connects Marvelous Designer and Unreal Editor, enabling direct communication and eliminating the need for further feedback and additional information. ### Using LiveSync in Unreal Engine In Unreal Engine, navigate to **Window > Close Slash MD LiveSync Editor**. The **Update** button allows users to instantly bring garments and avatars into the Close Slash MD LiveSync Editor. ### Saving Assets When ready to save, load the assets in the LiveSync Editor into the Unreal Engine browser. Select the desired assets in the LiveSync tree, then click the **Save** icon and choose to **Save As**, **Static Mesh**, or **Geometry Cache** to also bring in the cached animation. ## Set Dressing in Unreal Engine Set dress by dragging the file into the scene, and you can see your Marvelous Designer creation rendered in Unreal Engine. You can also bring MetaHumans to Marvelous Designer using LiveSync. ### Creating Animation with MetaHumans You can create animation by using **IK Retargeter** to drive the MetaHumans or by using Motion Capture Data or Keyframe animation directly in Unreal Editor. When opening the animation sequence, ensure that the Close MD LiveSync Editor is open. ## Exporting MetaHumans Pressing the **LiveSync** button in the top toolbar brings out the context menu. When ready, press the **Export** button. The MetaHumans Skeletal Mesh with animation is successfully imported into Marvelous Designer. ## Puckering Feature The **Puckering** feature makes it easy to showcase fine wrinkles in an outfit. You can create puckering on pattern outlines, internal line segments, and sewing lines, which will be visible on the 3D garment. ### Puckering Properties For seamline puckering, the puckering will appear on one or both segment lines, depending on the placement. In the puckering properties, open the puckering window from the **Window Selection** menu, where you can create, select, and modify puckering styles. ### Custom Texture Maps When selecting the material type as custom, you can add custom texture maps to be used as puckering in Marvelous Designer. ## Conclusion Marvelous Designer 2024 introduces a plethora of features that enhance garment creation, simulation, and integration with other software. These updates provide creators with powerful tools to optimize their workflow and produce high-quality digital fashion. ```
